_comment: The Card Ledger contract, asserted from both languages so the host and the
planner cannot drift apart about it (ADR 0022). The two contract runners
read this file: web/lib/cardLedgerContract.test.ts and the
Every case below is one the operator named or one that bit us:
reserving when Cards are free, refusing when they are not, releasing on
withdrawal, a Flown Card being reusable, and a Ledger that disagrees with
Cases share the Ledger below unless a case carries its own `ledger` object.
Adding a holding to it or reordering its pool changes what several cases
expect, so freeze it with the contract.

change_survived cases carry their own `base`; the shared Ledger above stays frozen. Ops: `reserve`/`release` are the planner's; `pool` and `verify` mirror the host's writers (publish_pool, merge_verified). `apply_to` on an `after` op names the Ledger it was built from: `base` (the stale copy) or `ours`.
The Ledger carries exactly `pool`, `holdings`, `verified_at`; a fourth top-level field needs both runners.

available._why: way finder 1 holds an unflown Mission. way finder 2 was flown, so it is reusable again.

reserve_two._why: A Spec that splits into two Missions takes the first two available Cards.

reserve_more_than_free._why: The operator's own case: every Card taken, another Mission Dispatched. Refused at Dispatch, naming what is in the way, rather than overwriting an unflown Mission at Load.

release_on_withdraw._why: Withdrawing a Spec gives its Cards back. What it holds is no longer current.

flown_holding_survives_release._why: A Flown holding is the record of what was flown; releasing its Spec must not erase it.

flown_mark_and_unmark._why: The operator's mark decides Flown: it frees the Card, and unmarking takes it back with the mark removed rather than falsified (ADR 0021, ADR 0022).

uncalibrated_card._why: The pool is what is calibrated, never what is hoped for. This Ledger's pool stops at way finder 5.

drift._why: The Ledger says one thing, the Controller holds another. Reported, never quietly corrected.

drift_silence._why: A Card the device was not asked about is not evidence of drift. Silence is not a disagreement.

stale_after_write._why: way finder 1 holds an unflown Mission whose Spec is no longer live, so the planner must say do not fly this. The Flown way finder 2 is not stale.

reservation_is_not_stale._why: A reservation that never reached the Controller is not stale on it: stale needs a written holding.

flight_order._why: Reserving records the flight order, so a row can say flight 2 of 3.

no_reservation_has_no_cards._why: A Spec that was never Dispatched holds no Cards, and the planner must say so by name rather than invent one.

concurrent_write_erased._why: Another writer wrote from before our Reservation landed, so their write erased ours. Both were told they succeeded (#152).

concurrent_write_kept._why: A later writer who kept our Reservation is not a conflict: only the Cards we changed are checked.

concurrent_write_same_card._why: The same Card given to someone else is our change lost, even though the Card is still occupied.

concurrent_pool_change_erased._why: The host published a newly calibrated pool; a planner write built from the copy read before it landed put the old pool back. A field we changed must survive, exactly as a Card must (#275).

concurrent_verified_change_erased._why: The host stamped verified_at; a planner write built from the copy read before the stamp landed erased it. The planner checked only holdings and called that success (#275).

concurrent_pool_write_is_not_a_conflict._why: The host published a pool while the planner reserved a Card from the copy read first. The pool is not ours to check: our Reservation survived, so this is not a conflict (#275).

concurrent_verified_stamp_is_not_a_confl._why: The planner reserved while the host stamped verified_at. The host's field is not ours to check: our Reservation survived, so this is not a conflict (#152).

flown_mark_only_null_unmarks._why: Unmarking is exactly null. A falsy-but-present value is not 'did not fly' and must not silently free the Card; availability still reads a falsy flown_at as unflown, so the Card stays held (#275).
